definitions.explanation: A short-legged Japanese table traditionally used for meals, around which family members would sit on the floor. Symbol of Showa-era family dining.

examples.japanese: ちゃぶ{台|だい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{囲|かこ}んで→囲む：02037_kakomu⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{食事|しょくじ}→食事：02087_shokuji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The family gathered around the chabudai for a meal.
There's still a chabudai at my grandfather's house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昭和|しょうわ}→昭和：28079_shouwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家庭|かてい}→家庭：12315_katei⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ちゃぶ{台|だい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一般的|いっぱんてき}→一般的：04784_ippanteki⟧⟦だった→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: The chabudai was common in Showa-era households.

notes:
CHARACTERISTICS:
・Short legs (typically 30-40 cm high)
・Usually round or square
・Can be folded and stored when not in use
・Used while sitting on the floor (⟦{畳|たたみ}→畳：02224_tatami⟧ or cushions)

CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE:
The ちゃぶ{台|だい} became popular in the Meiji and Taisho periods and symbolizes ⟦{昭和|しょうわ}→昭和：28079_shouwa⟧-era family life. It represents the image of the family gathered together for meals.

EXPRESSION: ⟦ちゃぶ{台|だい}{返|がえ}し→ちゃぶ台返し：29407_chabudaigaeshi⟧ (chabudai-gaeshi)
"Flipping the chabudai" - refers to dramatically overturning the table in anger, associated with the stereotypical strict father figure (⟦{頑固親父|がんこおやじ}→頑固親父：29408_gankooyaji⟧) in Showa dramas. Now used metaphorically for sudden, dramatic rejection or reversal.

MODERN CONTEXT: Most Japanese households now use Western-style dining tables, but ちゃぶ{台|だい} are still found in traditional settings and remain popular in the form of low ⟦{座卓|ざたく}→座卓：18328_zataku⟧ (floor tables) for ⟦{鍋|なべ}→鍋：01038_nabe⟧ (hot pot) gatherings.
